summary: Clear, well‑documented confirmatory study that executed a preregistered paired comparison of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline on a deterministic synthetic NetOps task pool. Execution and archival appear complete and internally consistent; the null/ceiling outcome (200/200 successes in both arms; no repair invocations) is transparently reported and correctly interpreted as a ceiling effect given the preregistered sampling and deterministic validator coverage. Reproducibility artifacts and hash manifests are comprehensive. No critical methodological or reporting defects were found that would block finalisation.
optional_revisions: Add a single concise table or boxed bullet summarising the preregistration power assumptions (target baseline failure = 0.20, target absolute reduction = 0.08) together with the observed baseline = 1.0 to make the power/design mismatch immediately visible to readers scanning the paper.

Add one short sentence in the Discussion that explicitly states the limitation that the shared_initial_generation design (preregistered) intentionally prevents the generator from adapting to verifier feedback; note how an alternate design that allows generator–verifier interaction could produce different operational outcomes and therefore remains an important axis for future work.
